<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a Dart monorepo (full-stack in the broad sense) hosting multiple related packages:  
     • shorebird_cli – a local CLI tool for developers  
     • shorebird_code_push_client & protocol – client-side libraries for communicating with the Shorebird CodePush API  
     • artifact_proxy & discord_gcp_alerts – standalone Dart servers  
     • jwt, redis_client, scoped_deps – utility libraries  
   - Its goal is to provide the shorebird developer experience: CLI orchestration, code‐push client, proxying Flutter artifacts, and forwarding GCP alerts to Discord.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level:  
     • .github/, scripts/ – CI, CD, e2e, deployment scripts  
     • bin/shorebird* – launcher scripts for the CLI  
     • packages/ – each subfolder is a standalone Dart package, grouped into:  
       – CLI (shorebird_cli)  
       – Client libraries (shorebird_code_push_client, shorebird_code_push_protocol)  
       – Server components (artifact_proxy, discord_gcp_alerts)  
       – Utility libraries (jwt, redis_client, scoped_deps)  
   - Each package follows the Dart “bin/”, “lib/”, “test/” pattern and has its own Dockerfile if it’s a server.

3. Examine the README  
   - Confirms this is a monorepo of interrelated Shorebird modules  
   - Describes each package’s purpose  
   - Points to docs and CI workflows

4. Creating the system design diagram  
   a. Main components to represent:  
      1. Developer Environment  
         - shorebird_cli (local binary)  
         - Dependencies: shorebird_code_push_client & shorebird_code_push_protocol libraries  
      2. Shorebird Backend Services  
         - (External/hosted) CodePush API – target of shorebird_code_push_client calls  
      3. artifact_proxy Server  
         - Proxies Flutter artifact downloads → Flutter artifact storage (e.g., pub.dartlang.org or GCS)  
         - Exposes HTTP endpoint  
      4. discord_gcp_alerts Server  
         - Subscribes to GCP Alert Pub/Sub push → forwards to Discord Webhook  
      5. Shared Libraries  
         - jwt, redis_client, scoped_deps – used as dependencies by the above components  
      6. CI/CD & Deployment  
         - GitHub Actions workflows that build, test, deploy artifact_proxy & discord_gcp_alerts  

   b. Relationships and interactions:  
      - shorebird_cli → (HTTP/HTTPS) → Shorebird CodePush API (uses shorebird_code_push_client & protocol)  
      - Developer’s Flutter toolchain → (HTTP) → artifact_proxy → (HTTP) → Flutter artifacts storage  
      - GCP Alert Pub/Sub → (push) → discord_gcp_alerts → (HTTP webhook) → Discord  
      - Shared libraries (jwt, redis_client, scoped_deps) are code‐level dependencies imported by CLI and servers  
      - CI/CD pipelines trigger Docker builds & deployments of server components  

   c. Architectural patterns / design principles:  
      - Modular monorepo: clear package boundaries, independent versioning  
      - CLI–Client–API separation: CLI depends on client lib, decoupled from backend  
      - Micro-services style: artifact_proxy and discord_gcp_alerts are self-contained servers  
      - Dependency injection via scoped_deps for runtime flexibility  
      - Use of code generation (build.yaml, *.g.dart) for protocol messages and config  

   d. Key technologies:  
      - Dart & pub for packages  
      - build_runner / codegen for JSON serialization (g.dart files)  
      - Docker + GitHub Actions for server deployment  
      - Zones/DI (scoped_deps) for managing scoped runtime state  
      - Redis client and JWT for auth/session management  

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram  
   - Emphasize layers:  
     • Client Layer (shorebird_cli + libs)  
     • API Layer (CodePush API – external)  
     • Server Layer (artifact_proxy, discord_gcp_alerts)  
     • Persistence / External Services (Flutter artifacts store, GCP Pub/Sub, Discord Webhook)  
   - Show the monorepo structure at a high level or in an inset to illustrate package boundaries  
   - For the CLI, highlight the built‐in commands, plugin points (commands/ folder) and how they depend on code_push_client & protocol  
   - For servers, show request flow: HTTP in → business logic → external backend/storage  

6. Diagram annotation recommendations  
   - Use distinct shapes/colors:  
     • Rectangles (green) for runtime components: CLI, servers  
     • Cylinders (blue) for external services: CodePush API, Flutter artifact storage, GCP Pub/Sub, Discord  
     • Oval/cloud icons (orange) for CI/CD and deployment pipelines  
     • Dashed rectangles to group shared libraries or the monorepo  
   - Label each arrow with protocol or library name (e.g., “HTTP + JSON via shorebird_code_push_protocol”)  
   - Indicate code‐level dependencies (dotted lines) vs. runtime calls (solid lines)  
   - Include legend for colors, shapes, line styles  

7. Detail & completeness  
   - Capture every package as a module in the monorepo inset  
   - Show how shared utilities (jwt, redis_client, scoped_deps) plug into both CLI and servers  
   - Don’t omit CI workflows: show GitHub Actions building the Docker images and deploying to dev/prod  
   - Ensure all external interactions (GCP, Discord, Pub/Sub, artifact storage) are represented  

By following these guidelines, the resulting system design diagram will give a comprehensive, accurate view of the Shorebird monorepo’s architecture, its runtime components, inter-component dependencies, and interactions with external services. 
</explanation>
